subject: Standby sizing verification and temporary gate for HelioNexus pilot
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@helionexus.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: provisional standby capacity for HelioNexus pilot

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our execs want to move the pilot into an internal staging run next month and asked whether Redwood can provision a provisional standby capacity window while contracts finish. High level ask: reserve up to 8x A100-80GB for inference (p95 latency target ~100ms) with burst to 12x for a 2-week training ramp. Pilot duration is 3 months, but they are open to a 6-month soft reserve if that helps you prioritize.

Can you confirm what you can lock today (soft hold vs committed), any lead times, and an estimate of unit economics (per-token or hourly for dedicated) so procurement can evaluate?

I can loop in procurement if helpful (cc'd).

—Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of ML Engineering, HelioNexus

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: provisional standby capacity for HelioNexus pilot

Folks —

Forwarding HelioNexus' ask. Short summary and what I need:
- They want a soft reserve: 8x A100-80GB, burstable to 12x for a short training window. Pilot scope 3 months, may prefer 6 months.
- Latency SLO: ~100ms P95 for inference; heavy peak during training ramp.
- Need: feasibility, fastest path to guarantee (soft hold token vs committed capacity), estimated lead time to move from soft->hard commit, and a conservative cost estimate (dedicated hourly / monthly).

I've attached their provisional sizing (helionexus_provisional_sizing.xlsx) they sent — contains expected QPS and seq lengths. Can you take inventory for us and advise recommended internal action (soft-hold, allocate from pool, or request a proc commit)?

Timeline: procurement is asking for an answer by EOD Thursday Pacific so they can start paperwork. If we can issue a soft hold (non-billing) today with token + 14-day hardening window, that would be ideal.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: provisional standby capacity for HelioNexus pilot

Jordan / team —

Inventory check completed (quick snapshot attached: fleet_snapshot_0903.csv). Short answer: we can support a soft hold for 8x A100-80GB in us-west-2 immediately from the standby pool, and we have an additional 4x A100-80GB in fragmented capacity across two racks that could be combined to hit 12x, but that requires a 10–14 day reallocation window and a maintenance-flavored migration to avoid noisy-neighbor effects.

Recommendations:
- Issue a "soft hold" token right away (non-billable) to reserve 8x for 14 days while procurement completes paperwork. Token: SOFTHOLD-HNX-09-03 (attached as softhold_token.txt).
- If HelioNexus wants an absolute guarantee to 12x during ramp, we need a short-term committed contract or to convert existing standing burst capacity (this would incur prorated billing for the period). Lead time: ~10–14 days to fully guarantee 12x and validate performance across racks.
- Expected impact on other late-stage deals: minimal if we keep to 8x soft hold; moving to guaranteed 12x may require shifting some standby allocations — I flagged OrionEdge and SkyForge in the internal tracker as potential knock-on effects (they're low probability to convert in the next 30 days but worth calling out).

Estimated costs (rough, for procurement):
- Soft hold (8x): $0 (reservation only)
- Committed dedicated (8x, monthly): ~$66,000 / month (billing model: reserved hourly equivalent; exact quote to be provided by finance)
- Committed dedicated (12x, monthly): ~$98,000 / month

I'll attach the snapshot and a short CSV. If you want me to pre-stage a node allocation (i.e., perform the rack balancing and perf verification), we can start the ops checklist but we'd need a signed addendum authorizing pre-provisioning (I can draft).

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Fleet Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@helionexus.ai>, HelioNexus Procurement <procurement@helionexus.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Standby sizing verification and temporary gate for HelioNexus pilot

Samir / team —

Thanks — Connor confirmed we can issue a soft non-billable hold for 8x A100-80GB immediately and outlined the path to guarantee 12x within ~10–14 days if you opt for a short-term commitment.

Next steps I propose:
1) We will provision the soft hold now (token provided internally).
2) I will send a short addendum that authorizes pre-provisioning (no charge until committed). If HelioNexus signs, Connor can begin rack balancing and perf verification so we can hit the 12x target quicker.
3) Procurement: if you can review the ballpark economics Connor included and confirm whether you want a 3-month or 6-month committed option, we will produce a formal quote and DocuSign addendum.

Attached: MOU_HelioNexus.pdf (draft MOU), and a DocuSign link in case you'd like to move quickly.

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MOU_HelioNexus.pdf (draft), docsign_addendum_link.txt
